title: Bacterial Leaf Blight of Rice (Xanthomonas oryzae)
content:
Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) is caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. It is widespread in irrigated and rainfed lowland rice, especially in South and Southeast Asia.

Symptoms: Water-soaked lesions at leaf margins that turn yellow to white and extend along the leaf. In severe cases, entire leaf dries up. 'Kresek' phase in seedlings causes complete wilting.

Favorable conditions: High humidity (80%+), temperatures 25-34°C, heavy rain with wind (bacteria spread through water and wounds), excess nitrogen, and dense planting.

Management: Plant resistant varieties (Swarna, IR64, Pusa Basmati). Balanced fertilization (avoid excess N). Avoid flooding. Seed treatment with Streptocycline. Foliar spray of copper oxychloride 2.5g/L at early disease appearance. Practice field sanitation.
content_hi:
जीवाणु पत्ता झुलसा Xanthomonas oryzae से होता है। यह सिंचित और वर्षा आधारित धान में व्यापक है।

लक्षण: पत्ती के किनारों से पानी से भीगे धब्बे, पीले-सफेद होकर फैलते हैं।

प्रबंधन: प्रतिरोधी किस्में लगाएं। संतुलित उर्वरक। स्ट्रेप्टोसाइक्लिन से बीज उपचार।
summary: Bacterial leaf blight causes water-soaked leaf margin lesions in rice. Spreads through water and wounds. Use resistant varieties and balanced nitrogen.
summary_hi: जीवाणु पत्ता झुलसा पत्तियों के किनारों से पानी से भीगे घाव पैदा करता है। प्रतिरोधी किस्में लगाएं।
actions: Inspect leaf margins for water-soaked lesions that turn yellow-white — this distinguishes BLB from brown spot.
Drain the field for 2-3 days — standing water spreads the bacteria between plants.
Avoid walking through the field when plants are wet — bacteria spread on hands and clothes.
Apply copper oxychloride 2.5g/L as foliar spray at first sign of disease — repeat after 10 days if rain continues.
For the next season, plant BLB-resistant varieties: Swarna, IR64, or Pusa Basmati 1509.
warnings: BLB is often confused with leaf blast. Check: BLB lesions start at leaf margins and are water-soaked. Blast lesions are diamond-shaped with gray centers.
Do NOT apply excess nitrogen — lush crops are much more susceptible to BLB.
